label: GPT-6.1 Terra
output:
To: ashbourne-terrace-chimney
Replying to: p05
Cc: none
Subject: Please do not enter 43

Mick, please don’t go into 43 at 9, and please don’t take your lad in either. Priya, please don’t give out a key for this. I know you’re trying to help, Mick, but putting props under the bay ceiling would mean standing under a holed roof with part of the chimney stack still loose above it. That’s a particularly dangerous place to be. The floors may also be carrying debris, and we don’t know how the damaged structure is carrying its loads now. Please don’t inspect the loft from inside either. This needs the council’s dangerous structures team, with the right access and precautions.

I’m a chartered structural engineer with IStructE, but I’m speaking here as a neighbour who looked from the opposite pavement, not as someone appointed to inspect or advise. This isn’t a commission and I have no professional indemnity cover for free advice.

At about 7 this morning I could see roughly 1.2 metres of the stack at 41 still standing and leaning towards 43, a hole in the front roof of 43, and a stepped crack above its bay. There were also loose slates along the gutter line of 43 and 45, directly above the footway. The council tape was across 43’s front garden, not the pavement.

Priya, I can’t say Mrs Doherty is safe from a look outside, and I couldn’t see the party wall between 43 and 45. It’s not my decision, but I would not sleep in her front room tonight. If she can stay with family until 45 has been checked, I think that would be better.

Please use the other side of the road until the council has attended, especially for the school run. The council already knows about the damage, but nobody has closed the footway. If you need to report the immediate pavement risk, dangerous structures out of hours can be reached through the council’s main number.

Jo, your cousin isn’t wrong that these terraces are generally robust, but this one has been damaged, which is a different matter.
